title: Nobin Boron (College Orientation Day)
subtitle: A Sea of 3,000 Notredamians, Raining Skies, and the Commanding Voice of Tetas Sir
body:
The Nobin Boron (orientation) at Notre Dame College was a mesmerizing, goosebump-inducing introduction to collegiate life. It was pouring rain that morning, and many of us assumed the program would surely start late. But at sharp 9:00 AM on the dot, the commanding, resonant voice of Tetas Sir (Prof. Tetas, Head of the Department of Physics) boomed through the speakers, instantly capturing the absolute silence of over 6,000 attendees.

Standing among 3,000 freshmen, all dressed in the pristine new college uniform with matching transparent college bags and holding flowers, I was left utterly speechless. The choreographic precision, clockwork punctuality, and grand organizational discipline of that morning were unlike anything I had ever witnessed. It was the unforgettable moment I realized what it truly meant to be a Notredamian—a shared memory every alumnus carries with pride.
